![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14068646/assets/e6351966b8cc79941da7c5cd1af6d590a20d62aaf72204fce96137b8676047f1.png)

A sketch of the phase space with nullclines and the corresponding direction field of tangents to the solutions of a system of differential equations is shown above (the tangents are not drawn to scale). Which of the following could represent the trajectory starting at the point marked on the graph?
worked_solution:
Let's sketch the trajectory.

- We start at the given point and go along with the flow (upward and slightly to the left) until the trajectory intersects the $x$-nullcline, where the tangents are vertical.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14068646/assets/56a39f156ab7cf44471d2984765e2b13fc46b4d1ec24805b92385d4d9b118da6.png)

- Next, the flow continues going upward but then turns to the right.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14068646/assets/297c4c1891788880cb43bb8b70126ead37c75dd0942d63ff79c12f6b3edd676d.png)

  

- After that, the trajectory goes to the right and slightly upward to infinity.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14068646/assets/80f1cb1edcbf35c4a3b87c0954a9302729f066d8dadf6205de7231343ab6e998.png)
